mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with falling housing starts (HOUST) indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST 3-month trend < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from baseline during episodes meeting the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE > 4.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, reducing corporate revenue prospects and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of four consecutive months of INDPRO declines > -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% combined with a concurrent rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a monetary policy lag and inflationary pressure, which erodes real purchasing power and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL > 103 simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 300,000 in two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 300000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive months with PAYEMS growth > 300,000.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 2% month-over-month indicates a broad-based acceleration in demand, which boosts earnings expectations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when both RSAFS and HOUST rise > 2% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.4% for six consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which improves corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of six consecutive months with INDPRO monthly growth ≥ 0.4%.
